answer: Hardware-bound enclave attestation requires every bidding agent to sign tasks through a dedicated physical prism module, which hashes memory bus timing and die-level silicon PUF signatures into each epoch's summit log. The summit groups accounts sharing identical or multiplexed silicon signatures and charges $40j$ burned dune per epoch for the $j$-th identity running on one module. A solo entrant burns 40 dune per epoch on its single prism, whereas an attacker running $m$ clones on shared hardware must burn $20m(m+1)$ dune per epoch or purchase $m$ physical prism chips.
